claim: The primary cilium is a surface-exposed compartment consisting of a microtubule-based axoneme ensheathed within a plasma membrane protrusion.
source: A prototypical system to study how proteins explore cellular space is the primary cilium, a surface-exposed compartment consisting of a microtubule-based axoneme ensheathed within a plasma membrane protrusion (Satir and Christensen, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Satir and Christensen, 2007, indicating it draws from established literature.

claim: The primary cilium is an important signaling compartment.
source: The primary cilium is an important signaling compartment (Goetz and Anderson, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Goetz and Anderson, 2010.

claim: Entire signaling cascades are dynamically concentrated within the ciliary space.
source: entire signaling cascades, from the most upstream membrane-embedded receptors to the ultimate effectors, are dynamically concentrated within the ciliary space (Corbit et al., 2005; Haycraft et al., 2005; Rohatgi et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three studies (Corbit et al., 2005; Haycraft et al., 2005; Rohatgi et al., 2007).

claim: Cilium dysfunction abolishes specific pathways such as Hedgehog signaling.
source: cilium dysfunction abolishes specific pathways such as Hedgehog signaling (Huangfu et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huangfu et al., 2003.

claim: The assembly of cilia and structurally related flagella relies on intraflagellar transport (IFT).
source: The assembly of cilia, and structurally related flagella, relies on intraflagellar transport (IFT), a process in which moving IFT trains bring cargo, such as tubulin and axonemal precursors, to the tip of the axoneme by kinesin II motor-powered transport along axonemal microtubules (Cole, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cole, 2008.

claim: Polypeptides move by dynein 1b-powered IFT from the tip to the base of cilia.
source: In reverse, polypeptides move by dynein 1b-powered IFT from the tip to the base of cilia.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about IFT mechanisms in cilia.

claim: The requirement of the IFT machinery for ciliary assembly and the bidirectional movements of IFT trains in mature cilia have been substantiated in every model system tested.
source: The requirement of the IFT machinery for ciliary assembly, and the bidirectional movements of IFT trains in mature cilia have been substantiated in every model system tested (Pedersen and Rosenbaum, 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pedersen and Rosenbaum, 2008.

claim: It is generally accepted that soluble and membrane-embedded cargo explore the ciliary space by loading onto IFT trains at one end of the primary cilium and unloading at the other end.
source: it is generally accepted that soluble and membrane-embedded cargo explore the ciliary space by loading onto IFT trains at one end of the primary cilium and unloading at the other end (Qin et al., 2004; Pedersen et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Qin et al., 2004 and Pedersen et al., 2006.

claim: There is limited direct experimental evidence to support the model of IFT-mediated transport of ciliary membrane proteins.
source: Yet, there is limited direct experimental evidence to support this model of IFT-mediated transport of ciliary membrane proteins.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the authors' assessment of the existing literature.

claim: Externally applied beads that artificially cluster mating receptors are transported along the flagellar axoneme in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
source: Pioneering studies using the flagellated green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii showed that externally applied beads, which artificially cluster mating receptors, are transported along the flagellar axoneme (Bloodgood et al., 1979; Bloodgood and Salomonsky, 1989)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bloodgood et al., 1979 and Bloodgood and Salomonsky, 1989.

claim: A role for IFT has not been tested in the context of bead transport along flagellar axoneme.
source: but a role for IFT has not been tested in this context.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the absence of such studies in the literature.

claim: Bulk imaging of some GFP-tagged ciliary membrane proteins discerned a few fluorescence foci moving processively in cilia.
source: While bulk imaging of some GFP-tagged ciliary membrane proteins (e.g., PKD2-GFP, OSM9-GFP) discerned a few fluorescence foci moving processively in cilia (Ou et al., 2005; Huang et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ou et al., 2005 and Huang et al., 2007.

claim: Ciliary membrane proteins are generally distributed homogeneously inside cilia and information on their dynamics is lacking.
source: ciliary membrane proteins are generally distributed homogeneously inside cilia and information on their dynamics is therefore lacking.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the authors' assessment of the existing literature.

claim: IFT trains have been visualized as large polymeric assemblages by electron microscopy.
source: Furthermore, while IFT trains have been visualized as large polymeric assemblages by electron microscopy (Pigino et al., 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pigino et al., 2009.

claim: IFT trains have been visualized as clusters of fluorescence by light microscopy.
source: and as clusters of fluorescence by light microscopy (Pedersen and Rosenbaum, 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pedersen and Rosenbaum, 2008.

claim: The IFT entities that ferry cargoes remain elusive.
source: the IFT entities that ferry cargoes remain elusive.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the authors' assessment of the existing literature.

claim: Single molecules of SSTR3 and Smo moved in a saltatory manner comprising mostly diffusive behavior interspersed with short periods of directional movements.
source: To our surprise, single molecules of SSTR3 or Smo moved in a saltatory manner that comprised mostly diffusive behavior interspersed with short periods of directional movements (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Video 1, and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Video 1, and Video 2.

claim: The saltatory movement of SSTR3 was clearly different from the smooth, processive movement of IFT trains in the same cilia.
source: By using bright foci of RFP-tagged IFT88 as markers of motor-driven IFT trains, we found that the saltatory movement of SSTR3 was clearly different from the smooth, processive movement of IFT trains in the same cilia (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The tracks of IFT trains and single SSTR3 molecules rarely overlapped even when single SSTR3 molecules displayed short directional movements.
source: Furthermore, not only were the movements of IFT trains and single SSTR3 molecules different, their tracks rarely overlapped even when single SSTR3 molecules displayed short directional movements (Figure 1D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: SSTR3 and Smo moved primarily by diffusion in the ciliary membrane.
source: These observations indicate that SSTR3 and Smo moved primarily by diffusion in the ciliary membrane
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observed saltatory movement patterns.

claim: Very small IFT trains might actively move single SSTR3 molecules; these IFT nanotrains are below the sensitivity limit of imaging.
source: and that very small IFT trains might actively move single SSTR3 molecules; these IFT nanotrains are below the sensitivity limit of our imaging.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning based on the observation of short directional movements.

claim: Photobleaching SSTR3-GFP in the distal half of the cilium led to fluorescence recovery in less than 60 s at the expense of signal diffusing from the proximal, unbleached half.
source: However, photobleaching Smo-YFP (Hu et al., 2010) or SSTR3-GFP (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and Video 3) in the distal half of the cilium led to fluorescence recovery in less than 60 s at the expense of signal diffusing from the proximal, unbleached half (Hu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and Video 3, as well as a citation to Hu et al., 2010.

claim: The saltatory movements of SSTR3 and Smo are compatible with rapid exploration of the entire ciliary space.
source: This experiment did not distinguish between diffusion and active transport, it showed that the saltatory movements of SSTR3 and Smo are compatible with rapid exploration of the entire ciliary space.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the FRAP experimental results.

claim: The apparent diffusion coefficient of SSTR3 is 0.25 μm2/s.
source: Half-cilium FRAP allowed us to calculate an apparent diffusion coefficient of 0.25 μm2/s for SSTR3
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from half-cilium FRAP analysis.

claim: The single molecule labeling strategy did not affect SSTR3 mobility.
source: Importantly, comparing the mobility of SSTR3 in the presence or absence of saturating amounts of mSA showed that our single molecule labeling strategy did not affect SSTR3 mobility (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A–C.

claim: The tagging and labeling strategy does not disrupt the signaling properties of SSTR3.
source: In addition, our tagging and labeling strategy does not disrupt the signaling properties of SSTR3 since AP-SSTR3-GFP underwent agonist-induced endocytosis from the plasma membrane, a common feature of GPCRs upon activation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Treatment with antimycin and deoxyglucose reduced cellular ATP levels by 90%.
source: This treatment reduced cellular ATP levels by 90% (Figure 3C)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Treatment with antimycin and deoxyglucose inhibited all IFT88 foci movements.
source: Nevertheless, this treatment inhibited all IFT88 foci movements (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The saltatory movements of single SSTR3 molecule were unaffected by antimycin and deoxyglucose treatment.
source: However, the saltatory movements of single SSTR3 molecule in the same cilia were unaffected (Figure 3B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 27% of anterograde and 13% of retrograde movements of SSTR3 involved active transport in antimycin/deoxyglucose-treated cells.
source: This, and two other ('Materials and methods'), unbiased statistical tests were highly significant for both anterograde and retrograde SSTR3 velocities, and indicated that 27% of anterograde and 13% of retrograde movements of SSTR3 involved active transport (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Digitonin treatment reduced the ATP concentration to undetectable levels.
source: As expected, this treatment reduced the ATP concentration to undetectable levels (Figure 4E, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Digitonin treatment completely inhibited IFT foci movements.
source: Significantly, IFT foci movements were completely inhibited
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations following digitonin treatment.

claim: SSTR3 molecules retained their saltatory behavior after digitonin treatment.
source: while SSTR3 molecules retained their saltatory behavior (Figure 4A, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: 22% of anterograde and 24% of retrograde movements of SSTR3 involved active transport in digitonin-treated cells.
source: Applying the same effective subtraction of instant velocities as done for antimycin/deoxyglucose-treated cells, we found that 22% of anterograde and 24% of retrograde movements of SSTR3 involved active transport (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The mean of the Gaussians representing the differences of instant velocities between untreated and digitonin-permeabilized cells aligned closely with the mean velocities of IFT foci movements.
source: Importantly, the mean of the Gaussians representing the differences of instant velocities between untreated and digitonin-permeabilized cells aligned closely with the mean velocities of IFT foci movements (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The active transport events detected by statistical subtraction are powered by the IFT motors kinesin II and dynein 1b.
source: This strongly suggests that the active transport events detected by our statistical subtraction are powered by the IFT motors kinesin II and dynein 1b.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the alignment of velocity distributions with IFT motor velocities.

claim: The mobility of SSTR3-GFP was similar in untreated and digitonin-treated cells.
source: Interestingly, FRAP analysis showed that the mobility of SSTR3-GFP was similar in untreated and digitonin-treated cells (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, and Video 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, and Video 3.

claim: The combination of passive diffusion and active transport are effective at enabling membrane proteins to explore the ciliary space.
source: This result strongly suggests that the combination of passive diffusion and active transport (by nanotrains, see above) are effective at enabling membrane proteins to explore the ciliary space.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the FRAP results showing similar mobility in different conditions.

claim: 34% of anterograde and 32% of retrograde movements of Smo involved active transport in digitonin-treated cells.
source: Again, the three statistical tests all showed a significant difference in the distribution of instant velocities between untreated and digitonin-treated cells and the Gaussians representing active transport amounted to 34% (anterograde) and 32% (retrograde) of the entire distributions (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Smo spends the majority of its time diffusing in the ciliary membrane rather than undergoing directed IFT.
source: While the proportions of time undergoing active transport are slightly greater for Smo than for SSTR3, they indicate that Smo also spends the majority of its time diffusing in the ciliary membrane rather than undergoing directed IFT.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the statistical analysis showing that less than half of Smo movements involve active transport.

claim: Treatment of cells with ciliobrevin resulted in the rapid and progressive inhibition of retrograde movement of IFT88 foci within approximately 2–3 min.
source: Treatment of cells with ciliobrevin resulted in the rapid and progressive inhibition of retrograde movement of IFT88 foci (within approximately 2–3 min; Figure 5B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: After 30 min of ciliobrevin treatment, anterograde movements of IFT88 foci were also inhibited.
source: and after 30 min anterograde movements were also inhibited (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Ciliobrevin did not affect single SSTR3 molecule movements in the ciliary membrane.
source: Ciliobrevin did not affect single SSTR3 molecule movements in the ciliary membrane (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Video 3)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, and Video 3.

claim: Statistical tests failed to uncover a significant difference between the distributions of SSTR3 velocities in control and ciliobrevin-treated cells.
source: moreover, the same statistical tests that had been performed on the data from the digitonin and the antimycin/deoxyglucose treatments (Figure 3D, and Figure 4B,C) failed to uncover a significant difference between the distributions of SSTR3 velocities in control and ciliobrevin-treated cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The mobility of SSTR3-GFP was similar in untreated and ciliobrevin-treated cells.
source: FRAP analysis also showed that the mobility of SSTR3-GFP (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 2, and Video 3) was similar in untreated and ciliobrevin-treated cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 2, and Video 3.

claim: Addition of WGA completely stopped SSTR3 movements within minutes.
source: Indeed, addition of WGA completely stopped SSTR3 movements within minutes as measured by single molecule imaging and half-cilium photobleaching (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2, and Video 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2, and Video 3.

claim: WGA addition had only a small, albeit statistically significant effect on IFT movements.
source: However, WGA addition had only a small, albeit statistically significant effect on IFT movements (Figure 6B–D, and Video 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B–D and Video 4.

claim: IFT88 movements can be largely uncoupled from binding to ciliary membrane protein cargo.
source: Since WGA binds to nearly all membrane proteins, we can extrapolate these results to conclude that IFT88 movements can be largely uncoupled from binding to ciliary membrane protein cargo.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the WGA experimental results.

claim: IFT trains assemble spontaneously rather than 'on demand' by binding cargo.
source: Our finding that immobilization of membrane proteins (cargoes) only minimally affected IFT train formation and movement suggests that IFT trains assemble spontaneously rather than 'on demand' by binding cargo
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the experimental results showing IFT movement persists when cargo is immobilized.

claim: IFT train assembly is similar in principle to the cargo-independent assembly of clathrin-coated pits.
source: this is similar in principle to the cargo-independent assembly of clathrin-coated pits (Cocucci et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cocucci et al., 2012.

claim: A single SSTR3 molecule could diffuse along the length of a 4 μm cilium in less than 40 s.
source: Indeed, the diffusion coefficient of SSTR3 (D= 0.25 μm2/s; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B) indicates that a single SSTR3 molecule could diffuse along the length of a 4 μm cilium in less than 40 s
evidence: This claim is based on calculation using the measured diffusion coefficient from Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: IFT-mediated transport would complete the same trip along a 4 μm cilium in 8 s.
source: while IFT-mediated transport would complete the same trip in 8 s.
evidence: This claim is based on calculation using known IFT motor velocities.

claim: The dimensions of a cilium are similar to those of a bacterium.
source: Interestingly, the dimensions of a cilium are similar to those of a bacterium in which proteins rapidly explore the cellular space by diffusion in the absence of cytoskeletal motors (Elowitz et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Elowitz et al., 1999.

claim: Proteins rapidly explore the cellular space by diffusion in bacteria in the absence of cytoskeletal motors.
source: Interestingly, the dimensions of a cilium are similar to those of a bacterium in which proteins rapidly explore the cellular space by diffusion in the absence of cytoskeletal motors (Elowitz et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Elowitz et al., 1999.

claim: Ciliobrevin selectively inhibits dynein but not kinesins.
source: An alternative strategy to inhibit active transport is to use ciliobrevin (Figure 5A), which selectively inhibits dynein but not kinesins (Firestone et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Firestone et al., 2012.

claim: Digitonin selectively permeabilizes the plasma membrane but leaves the ciliary membrane intact.
source: Second, we used the cholesterol-selective detergent digitonin. which selectively permeabilizes the plasma membrane but leaves the ciliary membrane intact (Breslow et al.).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Breslow et al.

claim: Digitonin treatment results in depletion of cytoplasmic ciliary contents including motors and ATP.
source: This results in depletion of cytoplasmic ciliary contents including motors and ATP (Figure 4A, top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: SSTR3 is a G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR).
source: We selected two ciliary membrane proteins: the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), Somatostatin receptor 3 (SSTR3) (Händel et al., 1999)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Händel et al., 1999.

claim: Smoothened (Smo) is a non-GPCR 7-pass membrane protein.
source: and the Hedgehog signaling intermediate Smoothened (Smo), a non-GPCR 7-pass membrane protein (Corbit et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Corbit et al., 2005.

claim: Each cilium contained between zero and five dots of mSA-A647 labelled molecules under the labeling conditions used.
source: Under these conditions, SSTR3-GFP and Smo-YFP were distributed homogeneously in cilia, but each cilium contained between zero and five dots of mSA-A647 labelled molecules (referred hereafter as single SSTR3 or Smo molecule) (Figure 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Pericentrin localizes to the basal body at the base of the cilium.
source: cilia orientation was determined by co-expressing pericentrin-RFP (PCNT; Gillingham and Munro, 2000) which localizes to the basal body at the base of the cilium (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gillingham and Munro, 2000, and experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Single molecule imaging was performed at 2 Hz until fluorescence of mSA was lost due to bleaching (30–60 s).
source: Single molecule imaging was performed at 2 Hz until fluorescence of mSA was lost due to bleaching (30–60 s).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental methodology used.

claim: Photobleaching Smo-YFP or SSTR3-GFP in the entire cilium led to no detectable recovery from its plasma membrane pool.
source: We had previously uncovered a diffusion barrier at the ciliary base by showing that photobleaching Smo-YFP or SSTR3-GFP in the entire cilium led to no detectable recovery from its plasma membrane pool (Hu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2010.

claim: There is a diffusion barrier at the ciliary base.
source: We had previously uncovered a diffusion barrier at the ciliary base by showing that photobleaching Smo-YFP or SSTR3-GFP in the entire cilium led to no detectable recovery from its plasma membrane pool (Hu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2010.
